{{primary sources|date=September 2021}}'''Stochastic Gronwall inequality''' is a generalization of [[Gronwall's inequality]] and has been used for proving the [[well-posedness]] of path-dependent [[stochastic differential equations]] with local monotonicity and coercivity assumption with respect to [[Uniform norm|supremum norm]].<ref name="mehri 2021">{{cite journal |title=A stochastic Gronwall lemma and well-posedness of path-dependent SDEs driven by martingale noise |journal=Latin American Journal of Probability and Mathematical Statistics|first1=Sima |last1=Mehri|first2=Michael |last2=Scheutzow |volume=18|year=2021|pages=193–209|doi=10.30757/ALEA.v18-09|s2cid=201660248|doi-access=free|arxiv=1908.10646}}</ref><ref name="von 2010">{{cite journal |title=Existence and uniqueness of solutions of stochastic functional differential equations|journal=Random Oper. Stoch. Equ.|first1=Max |last1=von Renesse|first2=Michael |last2=Scheutzow |volume=18|issue=3|year=2010|pages=267–284|doi=10.1515/rose.2010.015|arxiv=0812.1726 |s2cid=18595968|url=https://depositonce.tu-berlin.de//handle/11303/7235}}</ref>

== Statement ==
Let <math>X(t),\, t\geq 0</math> be a non-negative right-continuous <math>(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t\ge 0}</math>-[[adapted process]]. Assume that <math>A:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)</math> is a deterministic non-decreasing [[càdlàg]] [[Function (mathematics)|function]] with <math>A(0)=0</math> and let <math>H(t),\,t\geq 0</math>
	be a non-decreasing and [[càdlàg]] [[adapted process]] starting from <math>H(0)\geq 0</math>. Further, let <math>M(t),\,t\geq 0</math> be  an <math>(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t\ge 0}</math>- [[local martingale]] with <math>M(0)=0</math> and [[càdlàg]] paths.

Assume that for all <math>t\geq 0</math>,

<math> X(t)\leq \int_0^t X^*(u^-)\,d A(u)+M(t)+H(t),</math>
where <math>X^*(u):=\sup_{r\in[0,u]}X(r)</math>.

and define <math>c_p=\frac{p^{-p}}{1-p}</math>. Then the following estimates hold for <math>p\in (0,1)</math> and <math>T>0</math>:<ref name="mehri 2021" /><ref name="von 2010" />

*If <math>\mathbb{E} \big(H(T)^p\big)<\infty</math> and <math>H</math> is predictable, then <math>\mathbb{E}\left[\left(X^*(T)\right)^p\Big\vert\mathcal{F}_0\right]\leq \frac{c_p}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[(H(T))^p\big\vert\mathcal{F}_0\right] \exp \left\lbrace c_p^{1/p}A(T)\right\rbrace</math>;
*If <math>\mathbb{E} \big(H(T)^p\big)<\infty</math> and <math>M</math> has no negative jumps, then <math>\mathbb{E}\left[\left(X^*(T)\right)^p\Big\vert\mathcal{F}_0\right]\leq \frac{c_p+1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[(H(T))^p\big\vert\mathcal{F}_0\right] \exp \left\lbrace (c_p+1)^{1/p}A(T)\right\rbrace</math>;
*If <math>\mathbb{E} H(T)<\infty,</math> then <math>\displaystyle{\mathbb{E}\left[\left(X^*(T)\right)^p\Big\vert\mathcal{F}_0\right]\leq \frac{c_p}{p}\left(\mathbb{E}\left[ H(T)\big\vert\mathcal{F}_0\right]\right)^p \exp \left\lbrace c_p^{1/p} A(T)\right\rbrace}</math>;

== Proof ==
It has been proven by [[Lenglart's inequality]].<ref name="mehri 2021"/>
